blocks.prompt:
5 (i) Solve the following matrix equation for \(X\): \(2X - 3A = B\) if
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]
and
\[B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 4 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]
blocks.explanation:
A matrix equation: the unknown \(X\) is a matrix.
We solve it like a linear equation in algebra: make \(X\) the subject, then calculate.
Plan: \(X = \frac{1}{2}(B + 3A)\); find \(3A\), add \(B\), halve, then check in the given equation.
steps:
Given: \(2X - 3A = B\), with \(A\) and \(B\) of order \(2 \times 3\).
To find: \(X\).
Method: Matrix addition and scalar multiplication follow the usual rules, so we can move \(3A\) across and divide by 2, exactly as in \(2x - 3a = b\).

Make \(X\) the subject
\[2X = B + 3A\]
\[X = \dfrac{1}{2}(B + 3A)\]
Why: Add \(3A\) to both sides, then multiply both sides by the scalar \(\frac{1}{2}\). \(X\) has the same order as \(B\), \(2 \times 3\).

Find \(3A\)
\[3A = \begin{bmatrix}6 & 9 & -6 \\ -3 & 3 & 15\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Scalar multiplication: every entry of \(A\) is multiplied by 3.

Add \(B\)
\[B + 3A = \begin{bmatrix}2 + 6 & -3 + 9 & 1 - 6 \\ 5 - 3 & 4 + 3 & -1 + 15\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}8 & 6 & -5 \\ 2 & 7 & 14\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Entries in the same position are added.

Multiply by \(\frac{1}{2}\)
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 1 & \frac{7}{2} & 7\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Every entry is halved: \(-5/2 = -2.5\) and \(7/2 = 3.5\).

Check in the given equation
\[2X = \begin{bmatrix}8 & 6 & -5 \\ 2 & 7 & 14\end{bmatrix}\]
\[2X - 3A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 4 & -1\end{bmatrix} \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(2X - 3A\) gives back \(B\), e.g. \(8 - 6 = 2\), \(14 - 15 = -1\).

blocks.prompt:
5 (ii) Solve the following matrix equation for \(X\): \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = 0\) if
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\]
blocks.explanation:
A matrix equation with \(A^2\) in it.
We make \(X\) the subject: \(X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\), then calculate each part.
Plan: \(A^2\) by row-by-column multiplication, then \(5A\) and \(4I\), combine, and check by factorising.
steps:
Given: \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = O\), \(A\) of order \(3 \times 3\), \(I = I_3\).
To find: \(X\).
Method: Add \(X\) to both sides to get \(X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\). \(A^2\) means \(AA\).

Make \(X\) the subject
\[X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\]
Why: Adding \(X\) to both sides of \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = O\) moves it to the right.

Write \(A^2\), \(5A\) and \(4I\)
\[A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & 2 \\ 9 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[5A = \begin{bmatrix}10 & 0 & 5 \\ 10 & 5 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{bmatrix}\]
\[4I = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: \(5A\): every entry times 5. \(4I\): 4 on the diagonal, 0 elsewhere.

Combine
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}5 - 10 + 4 & -1 - 0 + 0 & 2 - 5 + 0 \\ 9 - 10 + 0 & -2 - 5 + 4 & 5 - 15 + 0 \\ 0 - 5 + 0 & -1 + 5 + 0 & -2 - 0 + 4\end{bmatrix}\]
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & -3 & -10 \\ -5 & 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Entry by entry: \(A^2\) minus \(5A\) plus \(4I\). The 4 is added only on the diagonal.

Check by factorising
\[X = (A - I)(A - 4I)\]
\[\text{Row 1: } (1, 0, 1)\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & -4\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= (-1,\ -1,\ -3) \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(A\) and \(I\) commute, so \(A^2 - 5A + 4I = (A - I)(A - 4I)\). Row 1 of \(A - I\) is \((1, 0, 1)\); multiplying by \(A - 4I\) gives row 1 of \(X\) again.
